report:
### Conclusion
There is **no scientific evidence** that taking ibuprofen worsens COVID-19 infections. Major global health authorities and clinical studies agree that ibuprofen is safe to use as directed for treating COVID-19 symptoms such as fever and pain.

### Evidence Behind the Claim
* **Origin of the View:** In March 2020, early in the pandemic, public concern spread after theoretical hypotheses suggested ibuprofen might upregulate ACE2 receptors (the receptor SARS-CoV-2 uses to enter cells) alongside early cautions issued by French health authorities.
* **Health Agency Stance:** Both the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the World Health Organization (WHO) evaluated the available evidence and clarified that there is no scientific link between ibuprofen or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and worsening COVID-19 disease. Neither organization recommends avoiding ibuprofen for COVID-19 symptoms.
* **Clinical Findings:** Subsequent observational studies and extensive clinical reviews found no association between ibuprofen use and an increased risk of severe disease, intensive care admission, or higher mortality among COVID-19 patients.

### Sources
* U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA): https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-alerts-and-statements/fda-advises-patients-use-non-steroidal-anti-inflammatory-drugs-nsaids-covid-19
* World Health Organization (WHO): https://www.who.int/news-room/commentaries/detail/the-use-of-non-steroidal-anti-inflammatory-drugs-(nsaids)-in-patients-with-covid-19
* Nationwide Clinical Study on Ibuprofen: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7537121/
* Narrative Review on NSAIDs and COVID-19: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10787-023-01309-7
